title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — condemnation & death correlatives; condemned to death not sin
pass_a_gloss: Certainly in this chapter condemnation and death are correlatives for Paul. We are condemned to death, not to sin. Death is not condemnation's cause but its effect. Sin—by which I mean hereditary corruption, as I have often said—is condemnation's cause, not its effect.
pass_b_english: Certainly condemnation and death are correlatives with the Apostle in this chapter. We are condemned to death, not to sin. Death is not the cause of condemnation, but the effect. On the contrary sin (but hereditary corruption is sin, as I have already often said) is the cause of condemnation, not the effect.
source_text: Certe condemnatio & mors sunt apud Apostolum hoc capite correlata. Condemnamur ad mortem, non ad peccatum. Mors non est condemnationis causa, sed effectum. Contra peccatum (est autem corruptio haereditaria, ut iam saepius dixi, peccatum) condemnationis causa, non effectum.

choices.choice: Condemned to death; death effect, hereditary sin cause
